title: Protecting Your Money & Making Informed Work Decisions
summary: Bring the unit together by learning how to protect payroll information, recognize suspicious requests, review job-related financial claims, and make informed decisions using verified information.
objectives: Recognize common warning signs involving payroll or financial information.
Protect sensitive information used for pay or direct deposit.
Evaluate job-related financial claims before acting on them.

vocab.def: An employer payment method that sends pay electronically to an authorized financial account.
A deceptive effort intended to obtain money, financial information, credentials, or other value.
Information such as account details, authentication credentials, or identifying information that requires careful protection.
Checking important information through an appropriate trusted or authoritative source before relying on it.

sections.heading: Payroll information deserves protection
sections.body: Account numbers, login credentials, tax forms, identifying information, and payroll records can contain sensitive information.

sections.heading: Urgency can be a warning sign
sections.body: Be cautious when someone unexpectedly demands money, passwords, account access, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or immediate financial action connected to a job.

sections.heading: Verify changes through trusted channels
sections.body: If you receive an unexpected request to change direct-deposit information, send money, or provide sensitive information, confirm the request through the employer's established process.

sections.heading: Financial readiness means asking good questions
sections.body: Understanding pay, deductions, benefits, budgeting, and financial safety can help you make better work decisions. It does not require a financial score or live access to your personal bank accounts.

practice.prompt: You receive a message claiming to be from payroll asking you to send your bank password immediately. What should you do?
practice.answer: Do not send the password. Verify the request through the employer's established payroll or human-resources channel.

practice.prompt: A job advertisement promises unusually high pay but asks you to pay money before you can begin work. What should you do?
practice.answer: Treat the request cautiously and verify the employer and opportunity before providing money or sensitive information.

quiz.question: What is the safest response to an unexpected payroll request for sensitive information?
options: Verify it through an established trusted employer channel before acting
Reply immediately with every requested credential
Send your bank password if the message looks official
quiz.answer: Verify it through an established trusted employer channel before acting

lab.objective: Review simulated workplace financial scenarios and identify normal payroll communication, questions needing clarification, and potential scam or security warning signs.
